name: research

args.task: Find any official NYC data, housing department reports, or statistics from 2026 showing the number of affordable housing units built, funded, or started under Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

result:
* HPD's Affordable Housing Production by Building dataset records 11,585 affordable units started across 539 projects with a project start date on or after January 1, 2026 ([NYC Open Data: Affordable Housing Production by Building](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/hg8x-zxpr)).
* For the baseline previous year (January 1, 2025 – December 31, 2025), HPD records 29,277 affordable housing units started across 854 projects ([NYC Open Data: Affordable Housing Production by Building](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/hg8x-zxpr)).
* Regarding completed construction, HPD records 15,660 affordable units completed across 474 projects with a building completion date on or after January 1, 2026 ([NYC Open Data: Affordable Housing Production by Building](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/hg8x-zxpr)).
* For the preceding baseline year (January 1, 2025 – December 31, 2025), HPD records 25,697 affordable housing units completed across 792 projects ([NYC Open Data: Affordable Housing Production by Building](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/hg8x-zxpr)).
* Checkbook NYC spending and contract data for the Department of Housing Preservation and Development was temporarily unavailable to query due to a temporary access blockage ([Checkbook NYC](https://www.checkbooknyc.com/)).

name: research

args.task: Search for news articles from 2026 describing the progress, status, setbacks, or achievements of Mayor Zohran Mamdani's plan to build 200,000 affordable homes over 10 years.

result:
* On May 26, 2026, Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani and Deputy Mayor Leila Bozorg released *“Block by Block: The Housing Plan for a New Era,”* a 10-year housing blueprint ([NYC Mayor's Office](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/05/mayor-mamdani-releases--block-by-block--the-housing-plan-for-a-n)).
* The plan sets a target to build 200,000 new affordable homes and preserve another 200,000 affordable homes over the decade ([NYC Mayor's Office](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/05/mayor-mamdani-releases--block-by-block--the-housing-plan-for-a-n)).
* The 10-year initiative is backed by a $22 billion capital investment in housing over its first five years ([NYC Mayor's Office](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/05/mayor-mamdani-releases--block-by-block--the-housing-plan-for-a-n)).
* Out of the 200,000 new affordable homes, the plan dedicates 30% for extremely low-income households and 20% for very low-income residents ([HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/nyc-affordable-housing-200000/)).
* Annual production is scheduled to scale from over 14,000 new homes in fiscal year 2027 to over 21,000 new homes annually by fiscal year 2031 ([HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/nyc-affordable-housing-200000/)).
* In August 2026, housing analysts noted that hitting the 10-year goal of 200,000 new and 200,000 preserved homes requires maintaining a consistent pace of 10,000 new and 10,000 preserved units every six months ([City Limits](https://citylimits.org/citys-affordable-housing-production-ticked-down-in-first-half-of-2026-and-what-else-happened-this-week/)).
* On October 1, 2026, Mayor Mamdani and Department of City Planning Director Sideya Sherman announced the first 12 community districts put on a fast track for affordable housing to advance the initiative ([NYC Mayor's Office](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/10/mamdani-administration-puts-12-neighborhoods-on-fast-track-for-a)).
